correctness.rationale: A cycle-by-cycle proof constructs the exact Laplace renewal quotient from independent Poisson switching and absorption in both phases. Brownian return from negative switching locations gives the sole order-sqrt(s) correction, with weighted killed-OU resolvent furnishing an integrable dominance; monotone Tauberian inversion yields the exact tail and fractional-moment threshold. For kappa>0 the OU backward hitting-time integral and splitting probabilities give the exact renewal mean; scaling erfcx and dominated convergence give the same amplitude times sqrt(pi/2). Discounted Dynkin on f(x)=x proves K=1-k*phi/((k+r)*p) and positivity/strictness. Reproducible finite-difference/quadrature script passes two independent parameter families but is not the proof.

value.rationale: The return trap at zero stiffness creates a genuine first-moment phase transition under arbitrarily rare noninstantaneous resets, despite finite baseline OU hitting time. This is not merely a numerical correction: the full survival tail, all fractional moments, sharp weak-confinement divergence and the identical physical amplitude are tied by a common first-cycle negative-position occupation mass. Such heavy-tailed return delays fundamentally change risk and protocol design even when average-time formulas at positive stiffness appear benign.
